clue.text: Careless chums must turn to run

indicators.note: the word for chums is turned round so that it reads backwards

parts.note: chums are pals
to run is to dash

explanation.surface: A warning that friends who ought to run will instead turn round, carelessly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'must turn' reverses PALS to SLAP before DASH is added.
explanation.definitionFit: Slapdash work is hasty and careless; the two words are synonyms.

clue.text: Safe after a botched rescue

indicators.note: a botched job is messed up, so the letters of the following word are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone is safe after a rescue attempt goes wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'botched' rearranges the six letters of RESCUE.
explanation.definitionFit: Secure and safe are synonyms: protected from danger.

clue.text: Most of this nut is needed by a large fish

definitions.text: Most of this nut is needed by a large fish

parts.words: Most of this nut is needed by a large fish
parts.note: the nut with its last letter dropped sits inside the name of a big river fish prized for food, which starts with S; a whimsical description of the nut by way of the fish

explanation.surface: A puzzling note that a big fish needs most of some nut.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop the final D and the remaining five letters, preceded by S, spell SALMON, the large fish: so the fish 'needs' most of the nut.
explanation.definitionFit: The clue points to a familiar edible nut, the kernel used in marzipan, through the fish whose name contains it.

clue.text: Benefit keeps two small daughters in a piece of cake

indicators.note: the benefit word keeps the daughters inside it, holding them within

parts.note: the dole is British slang for state unemployment benefit
D is the abbreviation for daughter, and two of them give DD

explanation.surface: Welfare money makes looking after two little girls easy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keeps' puts DD inside DOLE. THE DOLE is everyday British for unemployment benefit.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are informal idioms for something very easy to do.

clue.text: Just a little stuff to make music about

indicators.note: the music word goes about, or around, the stuff word

parts.note: to sing is to make music with the voice
stuff is matter, material

explanation.surface: Only a small amount of material is needed to make music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts SING around MATTER: S + MATTER + ING.
explanation.definitionFit: A smattering is a slight amount, a small sprinkling of knowledge or things.

clue.text: Cut nearly half a chop to char

indicators.note: nearly all of the cut word is used, its last letter lost

parts.note: to score is to cut lines into something

indicators.note: half a four-letter word is its first two letters

explanation.surface: A cooking instruction: trim a chop and then char it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nearly' trims SCORE to SCOR; 'half a' takes CH from 'chop'.
explanation.definitionFit: To scorch and to char are synonyms: to burn the surface of something.

clue.text: Coastal road spreads light on a broken chin, breaking one's heart

indicators.note: the jumbled chin breaks into the heart word, splitting it

parts.note: the heart of a thing is its core

indicators.note: a broken chin has its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A seaside road lit up for a heartbroken person with an injured chin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken' turns CHIN into NICH, and 'breaking' puts that inside CORE. 'spreads light on a' only joins the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A corniche is a road cut along a cliff or coast, especially on the French Riviera.

clue.text: See her turning up, since he would like warmed-up food

indicators.note: in a down clue the word is read from the bottom, so it comes out backwards

parts.note: since and as both mean because
he would contracts to he'd

explanation.surface: Someone notices a woman arriving, because a man wants leftovers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning up' reverses HER to REH; then AS and HE'D follow.
explanation.definitionFit: Rehashed food is reheated or reused leftovers, served again.

clue.text: Injure without being gentle

parts.note: to injure is to harm
less means without, as in 'a year less a day'

explanation.surface: Hurting someone without being kind.
explanation.definitionFit: Something harmless is mild and inoffensive, a near synonym of gentle.

clue.text: Wit requires trick to take in reporters

indicators.note: the trick word takes in, or contains, the reporters word

parts.note: to con is to trick
the media is the press, reporters collectively

explanation.surface: A clever person needs a ruse to fool journalists.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to take in' places MEDIA inside CON.
explanation.definitionFit: A wit is a person who makes clever jokes, as a comedian does.

clue.text: Protester topped bowman

indicators.note: topped means having its top, the first letter, removed

parts.note: a marcher is a protester on a demonstration

explanation.surface: A demonstrator beheads an archer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'topped' removes the first letter M from MARCHER.
explanation.definitionFit: An archer shoots with a bow, so bowman is a synonym.

clue.text: Fake sterling for this style of hair?

indicators.note: fake means not genuine, so the letters are reworked into a new form

explanation.surface: Wondering whether counterfeit money suits a particular hairdo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fake' rearranges the eight letters of STERLING. Sterling is British currency.
explanation.definitionFit: Ringlets are long spiral curls, a hairstyle.

clue.text: Young lady with a large prayer book

parts.note: a miss is a young unmarried woman
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: A girl carries a big book of prayers.
explanation.definitionFit: A missal is the book of texts used for Mass in the Catholic Church.

clue.text: Jesse, the robber, and William, the traitor, who wrote Ulysses

parts.note: Jesse James was the American outlaw and train robber
William Joyce, 'Lord Haw-Haw', broadcast Nazi propaganda and was hanged for treason

explanation.surface: Two villains, an outlaw and a traitor, combine to name an author.
explanation.walkthrough: Each famous figure supplies a surname; together they name the Irish novelist.
explanation.definitionFit: The Irish novelist published Ulysses in 1922, so the clue identifies him by his best-known book.

clue.text: Find the French among mixed bathers, gasping

indicators.note: the French article is placed among the jumbled bathers' letters
mixed means stirred up, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: les is the French plural form of the

explanation.surface: Spotting the French in a crowd of swimmers, out of breath.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mixed' turns BATHERS into BREATHS, and 'among' puts LES between BREATH and S. 'Find' only introduces the instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone gasping for air is short of breath, a synonym.

clue.text: Wrongdoer to propose concealing denouement

indicators.note: the propose word conceals, holding inside, the denouement word

parts.note: to offer is to propose
the denouement of a story is its end

explanation.surface: A criminal proposes something while hiding how it ends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'concealing' puts END inside OFFER: OFF + END + ER.
explanation.definitionFit: An offender is someone who commits an offence, a synonym for wrongdoer.

clue.text: Animal about to trot when climbing found an answer

indicators.note: in a down clue climbing means read upwards, so the whole assembly comes out backwards
the animal goes about, around, the trot word

parts.note: a deer is an animal
taken as written

explanation.surface: An animal about to trot uphill finds a reply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts TROT inside DEER to make DETROTER; 'when climbing' reverses it all.
explanation.definitionFit: To retort is to make a sharp reply, so retorted means came back with an answer.

clue.text: Just the house for a formal interview

definitions.meaning: in theatre, the house means the people watching a performance
a formal meeting with a monarch or pope, granted to a visitor

explanation.surface: Only the audience, assembled for an official meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Just' and 'for' only join the two meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both the spectators in a theatre and a formal hearing granted by someone important.

clue.text: Visited, if Quentin drops in, having got released to go outside

indicators.note: the released word is to go outside, around, the shortened name

parts.note: released means freed

indicators.note: the name drops the following little word, losing those letters

explanation.surface: Visiting somewhere once Quentin has turned up, now freed and allowed out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drops' removes IN from QUENTIN, leaving QUENT, and 'to go outside' wraps FREED round it: FRE + QUENT + ED.
explanation.definitionFit: To frequent a place is to visit it often, so frequented means visited regularly.

clue.text: Playwright has agreement with a company that's turned around

indicators.note: the whole run of words is turned around so that it reads backwards

parts.note: yes expresses agreement

explanation.surface: A dramatist agrees to a business that has turned itself round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned around' reverses YES + A + CO to give the Irish dramatist Sean O'Casey.
explanation.definitionFit: Sean O'Casey was an Irish dramatist, author of Juno and the Paycock.

clue.text: Poet was right to interrupt a wake

indicators.note: the right letter interrupts, breaking into, the wake word

parts.note: a wake is a watch kept over the dead, a vigil

explanation.surface: A poet was justified in disrupting a funeral gathering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to interrupt' puts R inside VIGIL.
explanation.definitionFit: Virgil was the Roman poet who wrote the Aeneid.

clue.text: Agreed to be seen in a football team from Manchester

definitions.meaning: the short name of Manchester's best-known football club, the Red Devils

explanation.surface: A football club showing a common front.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means in agreement, and it is the usual short name for Manchester's famous football club.

clue.text: Naughty boy absorbs part of the Bible

indicators.note: the boy's name absorbs, taking inside, the Bible part

parts.note: Eric is a boy's name
OT is the Old Testament

explanation.surface: A mischievous lad soaks up scripture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'absorbs' puts OT inside ERIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Naughty in its saucy, risque sense means sexually suggestive.

clue.text: Misery does not start when you get the sack

indicators.note: the misery word loses its starting letter

parts.note: misery is dejection, low spirits

explanation.surface: Being fired is a misery when it comes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'does not start' drops D from DEJECTION.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting the sack means being dismissed, thrown out of a job.

clue.text: Loving scoundrel hiding money

indicators.note: the scoundrel word hides the money word inside it

parts.note: a dog is a contemptible fellow, a scoundrel
tin is old British slang for money

explanation.surface: An affectionate rogue stashing cash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hiding' puts TIN inside DOG. TIN is old British slang for cash.
explanation.definitionFit: Doting means showing excessive fondness, so it fits loving.

clue.text: Perception is sure to break up a rowing team

indicators.note: the affirmation breaks up the rowing crew, sitting inside it

parts.note: a racing boat with eight oarsmen is called an eight
sure, as an answer, means yes

explanation.surface: Perceiving that a rowing crew is certain to split.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to break up' puts YES inside EIGHT: E + YES + IGHT.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyesight is the faculty of vision, one kind of perception.

clue.text: Looking more embarrassed, when going to and fro

indicators.note: the word reads the same going in either direction, forwards or back

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: Someone blushing deeper as they pace back and forth.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is a palindrome, signalled by 'going to and fro'.
explanation.definitionFit: Embarrassment makes the face flush, so a more embarrassed face is a deeper shade.

clue.text: Saved vehicle left outside

indicators.note: the left word goes outside, around, the vehicle word

parts.note: the political left is called red
a cycle is a vehicle

explanation.surface: A bike rescued after being abandoned outdoors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside' wraps RED around CYCLE: RE + CYCLE + D.
explanation.definitionFit: Recycled materials are saved from waste for reuse.
